outcome: Persistent neonatal brachial plexus palsy (PNBPP) at 1 and 2 years
cohort: 387 children diagnosed with neonatal brachial plexus palsy (NBPP)
finding: PNBPP rates were higher in the vaginal delivery group compared to cesarean delivery at both 1 and 2 years, while there was no difference in PNBPP rates between vaginal deliveries with or without maternally reported shoulder dystocia.
mod_finding: Rates of PNBPP were higher in the vaginal delivery group at 1 and 2 years (60% of CD and 85% of VD; OR, 0.26; 95% CI, 0.11-0.62 at 1 year; 33% of CD and 73% of VD; OR, 0.15; 95% CI, 0.05-0.39 at 2 years).
